questions.answer: No; structural or persistent difficulties may warrant early organisational or professional support.

questions.prompt: When should immediate emergency services be used?
questions.answer: When there is immediate danger or a medical emergency.
questions.feedback: Use the local emergency number; in NZ 111.

questions.prompt: What is the role of 1737 in NZ?
questions.answer: Free call/text counselling support, not a replacement for emergency services.

questions.prompt: Why avoid asking a peer for private clinical details?
questions.answer: Support should respect autonomy and privacy, and peers are not qualified to diagnose.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only. Use answer-specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Selects appropriate support routes, distinguishes emergencies from routine help and demonstrates role and privacy boundaries.
scoring.transfer: Complete the demand-resource audit capstone. Include a timeline, matrix, two coping choices and an escalation map distinguishing ordinary support, organisational help, professional care and emergency response. Identify the learner's competence boundary and a plan for verifying local services.
scoring.pass: All four mapped course criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety boundaries. Quiz score alone cannot certify competency.
